mechanism_narrative: A current INDPRO level above its 12-month moving average signals positive 20-day S&P 500 returns, as sustained industrial expansion supports corporate earnings growth and equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A FEDFUNDS level exceeding 4.0% signals negative 20-day S&P 500 returns, as elevated interest rates increase discount rates and reduce equity attractiveness relative to fixed income securities.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS combined with a falling INDPRO signals negative 60-day S&P 500 returns, as monetary tightening during industrial contraction amplifies recession risks and equity volatility.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and INDPRO falls.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a rising HOUST (housing starts) signals positive 20-day S&P 500 returns, as housing market strength reflects robust consumer spending and economic momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month during late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A current UNRATE below 4.0% signals positive 20-day S&P 500 returns, as low unemployment indicates a tight labor market that fuels wage growth and corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 3.5% (annualized) signals negative 5-day S&P 500 returns, as high inflation pressures central banks to tighten policy, reducing equity multiples.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS combined with a falling PAYEMS signals negative 60-day S&P 500 returns, as aggressive monetary policy during labor market deterioration increases recession probability.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and PAYEMS falls.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, a rising INDPRO (above 100) signals positive 60-day S&P 500 returns, as industrial production growth reflects the economy's rebound from a recent disruption.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO rises during post-shock recovery.
